intro: Wrestling may be the oldest sport people still play. Painters in Egypt showed it on tomb walls about 4,000 years ago. Storytellers in Mesopotamia put it in the Epic of Gilgamesh. Festivals in Mongolia, Turkey and Iran still hold it today.

Schools and leagues came much later. Weight classes, padded mats and match clocks are all modern. In Illinois, the IHSA crowned its first state wrestling champions in 1937. Girls got their own state finals in 2022.

In this unit you will line up old evidence and new records. You will be able to say what a date measures. You will tell a legend from a record. You will explain how a state association turned an old practice into a school sport.
bigQuestion: When did wrestling begin, and when did it become a school sport?

title: Wrestling Older Than the League

chapters.title: Holds Before Stadiums
chapters.bigQuestion: How do we know people wrestled thousands of years before any league or school team?

story.title: Two Wrestlers in a Glass Case
story.kicker: A small figure of two wrestlers is far older than any gym clock.
paragraphs: A museum hall is quiet. In one glass case stands a small metal figure. It shows two wrestlers gripping each other. Each one balances a jar on his head. A label says it was found at Khafajah, in today's Iraq.

The label gives a date of about 2600 BCE. That is more than 4,500 years ago. The people who made it were Sumerians. They lived between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. Nobody wrote down who these two men were.
Down the hall, a school trophy case holds a newer object. It is a plaque from a high school wrestling tournament. It names a weight class and a year. It was made less than a hundred years ago.

Both objects show wrestling. But they come from very different rooms. The old figure comes from a world with no weight classes and no clock. The plaque comes from a school sport with a rule book. This chapter follows wrestling from old walls to the modern mat.
story.think: What can an old figure tell us about wrestling, and what can it not tell us?

lessons.title: The Tombs at Beni Hasan
lessons.mainIdea: Tomb paintings at Beni Hasan in Egypt show hundreds of wrestling pairs from about 4,000 years ago.
reading: Beni Hasan is a row of rock tombs in Middle Egypt. The tombs are cut into cliffs on the east bank of the Nile River. Local governors were buried there about 4,000 years ago. Historians call that time the Middle Kingdom.

Painters covered some tomb walls with rows of *wrestling* pairs. One wall shows hundreds of pairs, one after another. Each pair is painted in a different grip. Painters used a darker and a lighter skin color so viewers could tell the two men apart.

The paintings do not tell us the rules. They do not say who won. But they are *evidence*, or proof, that wrestling mattered in Egypt long ago. Governors chose it for the walls of their own tombs, next to scenes of farming, hunting and soldiers.

words.d: a contest where two people grip each other and try to control or pin the other
something real, like an object or a record, that shows a fact is true

look.title: A Wall of Pairs

lessons.title: A Wrestling Match in a Story
lessons.mainIdea: The Epic of Gilgamesh, an old story from Mesopotamia, includes a famous wrestling match.
reading: *Mesopotamia* was the land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. Today most of it is in Iraq. People there wrote on clay tablets with a reed pen. One long story they copied is the *Epic of Gilgamesh*.

In the story, Gilgamesh is the proud king of the city of Uruk. The gods make a wild man named Enkidu to match him. The two meet at a doorway and wrestle. Neither can easily beat the other. After the match, they become close friends.

The Epic is a story, not a sports report. Gilgamesh may have been a real early king, but the match is legend. Still, the story tells historians something true. The people who wrote it knew wrestling well enough to use it as a test of strength.

a long old story from Mesopotamia about King Gilgamesh of Uruk, written on clay tablets
an old story told as if it happened, which historians cannot prove

check.why: In the Epic of Gilgamesh, the king wrestles the wild man Enkidu.

lessons.title: The Greek Wrestling School
lessons.mainIdea: Ancient Greeks trained in a building called a palaestra and added wrestling to the Olympic Games.
reading: In ancient Greece, many cities had a *palaestra*. It was a building with an open courtyard for wrestling. Young men trained there under a teacher. The word comes from pale, the Greek word for wrestling.

Greek writers said wrestling joined the *Olympic Games* in 708 BCE. The Games were held at Olympia every four years. Wrestling was also one of the five events of the pentathlon. Winners got a crown of olive leaves, not a gold medal.

The most famous Greek wrestler was Milo of Croton. Croton was a Greek city in southern Italy. Ancient writers said Milo won at Olympia six times in the 500s BCE. Many stories about his strength grew later and are legends.

words.d: a building in ancient Greece with a courtyard for wrestling practice
the ancient games held every four years at Olympia, in Greece

look.title: Two Rooms for Wrestling
look.text: Picture an open courtyard in a Greek city, 2,500 years ago. The floor is sand. A teacher watches young men. Now picture a high school wrestling room today. The floor is a padded mat. A clock hangs on the wall.
look.prompt: Name one way these two rooms are alike and one way they are different.

check.why: Greek writers gave 708 BCE as the year wrestling was added at Olympia.

check.q: What did ancient Olympic winners receive?
check.why: Winners at Olympia got a crown of olive leaves.

lessons.title: Sumo at the Japanese Court
lessons.mainIdea: Sumo has old roots in Japan, from legends to court festivals to paid tournaments.
reading: *Sumo* is Japan's best-known wrestling. An old book called the Nihon Shoki was finished in 720 CE. It tells a legend of a match between two strong men. One of them, Nomi no Sukune, is honored in sumo as a founder. Historians treat the tale as legend.

Records show sumo at the emperor's court in the Heian period, which began in 794. Wrestlers came from the provinces for a yearly court festival. The contests were part of court ceremony, with music and officials.

Later, in the Edo period (1603 to 1868), sumo became a paid public show. Wrestlers joined stables called *heya*. Tournaments drew crowds in cities like Edo, now Tokyo. The rule that a wrestler loses by leaving the ring comes from this long history.

words.d: a Japanese form of wrestling with a long history at court and in public tournaments
a sumo stable, the group and home where professional sumo wrestlers live and train

check.q: How do historians treat the story of Nomi no Sukune?

check.q: When did sumo become a paid public show in cities?

lessons.title: Wrestling at Naadam
lessons.mainIdea: In Mongolia, wrestling called bökh is one of the three games of the Naadam festival.
reading: Mongolia is a country in Central Asia between Russia and China. Its biggest summer festival is *Naadam*. The festival has three main contests. They are horse racing, archery and wrestling.

Mongolian wrestling is called *bökh*. Matches take place on open grass, not inside a ring. There are no weight classes. Wrestlers wear a small open jacket and short trunks. Winners earn titles such as falcon, elephant, lion and titan.

Before and after a match, wrestlers perform a dance that many Mongolians call the eagle dance. It honors the festival and the other wrestler. In 2010, UNESCO, a United Nations body, listed Naadam as world cultural heritage.

words.d: Mongolia's summer festival of horse racing, archery and wrestling
Mongolian wrestling, held on open grass at Naadam
a United Nations body that lists and protects world culture and heritage

lessons.title: Oil Wrestling at Kırkpınar
lessons.mainIdea: Turkey's Kırkpınar oil wrestling festival in Edirne says it has been held since 1362.
reading: Edirne is a city in the far northwest of Turkey. Every summer it hosts *Kırkpınar*, a festival of oil wrestling. Turkish oil wrestling is called yağlı güreş. Wrestlers cover themselves in olive oil before they meet.

The festival's own history says it began in 1362. That would make it one of the oldest sports events still held. Historians note that early records are thin, so the exact start date is a claim, not a proven fact.

Wrestlers wear heavy leather trousers called *kispet*. The overall winner earns the title başpehlivan, or chief wrestler, and a golden belt. UNESCO listed the Kırkpınar festival as world cultural heritage in 2010.

words.d: a yearly oil wrestling festival held in Edirne, Turkey
the heavy leather trousers worn in Turkish oil wrestling

look.title: A Claim and a Record

look.prompt: How can both statements be true? What would you need to check?

check.why: Kırkpınar is held each summer in Edirne, in northwest Turkey.

choices: the date is on a gold belt
check.why: The festival says 1362, but early records are thin, so the date cannot be fully proved.

choices: leather trousers worn in oil wrestling
check.why: Kispet are the heavy leather trousers of Turkish oil wrestlers.

lessons.title: The House of Strength in Iran
lessons.mainIdea: In Iran, the zurkhaneh is a traditional gym where wrestling and exercise are joined with poetry and drums.
reading: In Iran, a *zurkhaneh* is a traditional gym. The Persian word means house of strength. The training area is a sunken pit, often with eight sides. Men train in it while others watch from around the edge.

A leader called the *morshed* sits above the pit. He beats a drum and rings a bell. He also sings or recites verses, often from the Shahnameh. The Shahnameh is a long Persian poem of kings and heroes by Ferdowsi, finished around 1010 CE.

The tradition is called koshti pahlevani, or heroes' wrestling. It honors good character, like humility and helping others. In 2010, UNESCO listed the rituals of Pahlevani and the zurkhaneh as world cultural heritage.

words.d: an Iranian traditional gym; the name means house of strength
the leader who drums, rings a bell and recites poetry in a zurkhaneh

look.title: A Drum Above the Pit
look.text: Men stand in a sunken pit with eight sides. Above them, a man sits at a raised seat with a drum. He recites old lines of poetry about heroes. The men move in time with the drum.
look.prompt: Why might a gym use poetry about heroes? What does it teach besides strength?

check.why: Zurkhaneh is Persian for house of strength.

check.q: What does the morshed do?
choices: drums, rings a bell and recites poetry
check.why: The morshed leads the zurkhaneh with drum, bell and verses.

check.q: What is the Shahnameh?

check.why: The Shahnameh is Ferdowsi's long Persian poem of kings and heroes.

lessons.title: Wrestling in the Modern Olympics
lessons.mainIdea: Wrestling was in the first modern Olympics in 1896, and weight classes arrived soon after.
reading: The first modern *Olympics* were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Wrestling was on the program. There was only one wrestling event. There were no *weight classes*, so a small man could face a much larger one. Carl Schuhmann of Germany won.

The 1904 Olympics were held in St. Louis, Missouri. That year added freestyle wrestling, with several weight classes. Almost every wrestler was American. A weight class groups wrestlers who weigh about the same.
The 1896 event followed Greco-Roman rules. In Greco-Roman wrestling, holds below the waist are not allowed. Freestyle allows them. Both styles have been part of most Olympics since.

words.d: the modern international games, first held in Athens in 1896
a group of wrestlers who weigh about the same and face each other
an Olympic wrestling style that does not allow holds below the waist

lessons.title: One Body for World Rules
lessons.mainIdea: Since 1912, an international federation has written wrestling's world rules.
reading: A *federation* is a group that joins many clubs or countries under one set of rules. Wrestling's world federation was founded in 1912. For most of its life it used a French name, shortened to FILA.

In 2014, FILA changed its name to *United World Wrestling*. It sets the rules for Olympic and world championship wrestling. It decides the weight classes, the length of a match and how points are scored.

Women's wrestling grew through the federation's world championships before the Olympics. Women's freestyle joined the Olympic Games in Athens in 2004. That was 108 years after men first wrestled at the modern Games.

words.d: a group that joins many clubs or countries under one set of rules
the world body for wrestling rules, founded in 1912 and called FILA until 2014

look.title: Who Writes the Rules?
look.text: At a festival in Mongolia, elders and custom decide how a match goes. At the Olympics, a printed rule book from a world federation decides. Both are wrestling. Only one rule book is the same in every country.
look.prompt: What does a world rule book make possible that local custom does not?

check.why: A federation joins many members under one set of rules.

check.why: The world body used the name FILA until it became United World Wrestling in 2014.

check.q: When did women's freestyle join the Olympics?
check.why: Women's freestyle wrestling joined the Olympic Games in Athens in 2004.

lessons.title: The Mat, the Scale and the Clock
lessons.mainIdea: School wrestling added a padded mat, a scale and a clock to a very old practice.
reading: Old wrestling happened on sand, grass or packed earth. School wrestling in the United States happens on a padded *mat*. A circle painted on the mat marks where the match counts. The padding was added for safety.

Before a school meet, each wrestler steps on a scale at the *weigh-in*. The weigh-in places each wrestler in a weight class. This lets students of many sizes compete fairly. It is a rule that Beni Hasan and Naadam never needed.

High school matches in the United States follow the rule book of the National Federation of State High School Associations, called the NFHS. Its matches have three periods of two minutes each. A clock is one of the newest parts of wrestling's very long history.

words.d: the padded floor where school and Olympic wrestling take place
the time before a meet when each wrestler is weighed to set a weight class
the National Federation of State High School Associations, which writes rule books for school sports

chapters.title: Illinois 1937
chapters.bigQuestion: What did 1937 start in Illinois, if people had wrestled there long before?

story.title: A Program Under a State Seal
story.kicker: A tournament program from 1937 marks a beginning, but not the beginning of wrestling.
paragraphs: Picture a thin paper program from the spring of 1937. At the top is the seal of the Illinois High School Association. Below it are the words State Wrestling Tournament. It is the first one the association ever held.

Inside, the pages are lists. Each list is headed by a weight. Under each weight are names of high school boys and the towns of their schools. Next to the lists are blank lines for scores. Someone at the tournament will fill them in with a pencil.

The paper is new in 1937. Wrestling in Illinois is not. More than a hundred years earlier, a young Abraham Lincoln wrestled in the village of New Salem. In 1908, crowds in Chicago watched a famous professional match.
So what does the program mark? It marks the day wrestling became a state school sport with a champion in each weight. That is a real change. It is just not the first time anyone in Illinois wrestled.
story.think: What is the difference between the first state champion and the first person to wrestle?

lessons.title: What the IHSA Is
lessons.mainIdea: The Illinois High School Association, founded in 1900, runs state contests for Illinois high schools.
reading: The *IHSA* is the Illinois High School Association. It was founded in 1900. Member high schools agreed to follow shared rules for school contests. Before that, each school or town could set its own rules.
An *association* is a group of members who agree to work under the same rules. The IHSA decides who may play, which rules apply and how state tournaments are run. It also crowns state champions.

The IHSA did not start with wrestling. Its first state contests were in other sports. For example, boys tennis crowned its first state champion in 1912. Each sport joined the state series in its own year.

words.d: the Illinois High School Association, founded in 1900, which runs state high school contests
a group of members who agree to work under the same rules

look.title: IHSA Years
look.cite: Illinois High School Association, records on ihsa.org

check.why: The Illinois High School Association was founded in 1900.

lessons.title: The First State Champions
lessons.mainIdea: In 1937, the IHSA crowned its first state wrestling champions, one in each weight class.
reading: In 1937, the IHSA held its first state wrestling tournament for boys. It named a *state champion* in each weight class. A state champion is the winner of the last round of the state tournament.
The tournament used a *bracket*. A bracket is a chart that shows who meets whom in each round. Winners move to the next line. The last two wrestlers in each weight meet for the title.

The IHSA keeps lists of state champions in its records. Those lists begin with 1937 for wrestling. That is why historians of Illinois school sports use 1937 as the start date. It is a date for a school contest, not for a practice.

words.d: the winner of the final round of a state tournament
a chart showing who meets whom in each round of a tournament

look.title: Reading a Bracket
look.text: A chart has eight names on the left. Lines join them in pairs. The winners' names move to four lines, then two, then one. The name on the last line is the champion.
look.prompt: How many rounds does it take to go from eight names to one?

check.q: What happened in Illinois in 1937?
choices: the IHSA held its first state wrestling tournament
check.why: In 1937, the IHSA crowned its first state wrestling champions.

check.q: What is a bracket?
choices: a chart of who meets whom in each round
check.why: A bracket shows the pairings and rounds of a tournament.

check.q: Why do Illinois records start wrestling in 1937?
choices: that is the first year of the IHSA state tournament
check.why: The IHSA lists begin with its first state tournament in 1937.

lessons.title: A Rule Book for Many States
lessons.mainIdea: State associations share rule books through a national federation, the NFHS.
reading: Illinois is not the only state with a high school association. Every state has one. In 1920, a few Midwest state associations formed a national group. Today it is the *National Federation of State High School Associations*, or NFHS.

The NFHS writes rule books for many school sports, including wrestling. State groups like the IHSA use those books. That way, a wrestling match in Illinois follows nearly the same rules as one in Ohio.

A shared rule book is a *standard*. A standard is a rule many groups agree to use. Standards let schools from different towns meet fairly. They also let a record in one state be compared with a record in another.

words.w: National Federation of State High School Associations
words.d: the NFHS, formed in 1920, which writes rule books used by state high school groups
a rule that many groups agree to use the same way

look.prompt: Why does a shared rule book matter when two strangers compete?

lessons.title: Lincoln at New Salem
lessons.mainIdea: Abraham Lincoln wrestled at New Salem, Illinois, around 1831, more than a century before the first state tournament.
reading: In 1831, young Abraham Lincoln moved to *New Salem*, a small village on the Sangamon River in Illinois. He worked in a store. In frontier villages, wrestling was a common way for young men to test strength and win respect.

Stories say Lincoln wrestled Jack Armstrong, leader of a local group called the Clary's Grove boys. People who knew Lincoln told different versions later. Some said it ended in a draw. All agree that Lincoln earned the group's respect.

Many stories about Lincoln's wrestling were told after he became famous. Historians treat the details carefully. Still, the National Wrestling Hall of Fame honors Lincoln. The New Salem village has been rebuilt as a state historic site near Petersburg.

words.d: a village on the Sangamon River in Illinois where Lincoln lived in the 1830s
the edge of settled land in the early United States, where towns were new and small

look.title: Two Versions of One Match
look.text: One old neighbor says Lincoln won the match with Jack Armstrong. Another says it was a draw. Both told their stories many years later, after Lincoln became president.
look.prompt: Why might people remember a match differently after the wrestler became famous?

check.why: Lincoln lived in New Salem, a village on the Sangamon River, in the early 1830s.

check.q: Why do historians treat the Lincoln wrestling stories carefully?
choices: many were told after he became famous
check.why: Many stories were told later, and they do not all agree.

check.q: What does the New Salem story show about 1937?
choices: people wrestled in Illinois long before 1937
check.why: Lincoln wrestled around 1831, more than a century before the first state tournament.

lessons.title: A Famous Match in Chicago
lessons.mainIdea: In 1908 and 1911, Frank Gotch and George Hackenschmidt drew huge crowds to professional matches in Chicago.
reading: *Professional* wrestlers wrestle for money. In the early 1900s, one of the most famous was Frank Gotch. He was a farm boy from Humboldt, Iowa. His great rival was George Hackenschmidt, a strongman born in Estonia, then part of the Russian Empire.

In April 1908, Gotch and Hackenschmidt met at the Dexter Park Pavilion in Chicago. The pavilion stood near the city's Union Stock Yards. Gotch won and was called world heavyweight champion. Newspapers across the country reported the result.

They met again in Chicago on Labor Day in 1911. This time the match was at Comiskey Park, the White Sox ballpark. A very large crowd came. Gotch won again. These matches show that Chicago was a wrestling city decades before 1937.

words.d: doing something as a paid job; professional wrestlers wrestle for money
a person someone competes against again and again

check.why: Professionals wrestle as a paid job; IHSA wrestlers are high school students.

lessons.title: Clubs and Colleges
lessons.mainIdea: Amateur clubs and colleges held wrestling championships before Illinois high schools did.
reading: An *amateur* competes without being paid. In 1888, clubs across the United States formed the Amateur Athletic Union, or AAU. The AAU held national championships in many sports, including wrestling. Athletes from city athletic clubs entered.

Colleges also had wrestling teams. The National Collegiate Athletic Association, the *NCAA*, held its first national wrestling championships in 1928. College matches followed their own rule book, a little different from high school rules.

So by 1937, Illinois wrestlers could already compete in clubs, colleges and professional shows. The IHSA tournament added one more room: the high school. Each room had its own leaders, rule book and champions.

words.d: a person who competes without being paid
the National Collegiate Athletic Association, which runs college sports championships

lessons.title: A First Title, Not a First Hold
lessons.mainIdea: The year 1937 marks the start of a school contest, not the start of wrestling.
reading: Historians ask what a date measures. The year 1937 measures when the IHSA first crowned wrestling champions. It does not measure when people first wrestled. For that, we look at *artifacts* like the Beni Hasan tomb paintings, about 4,000 years old.
It helps to line dates up. Beni Hasan is about 4,000 years old. Wrestling joined the ancient Olympics in 708 BCE. Lincoln wrestled at New Salem around 1831. The IHSA tournament came in 1937.
Each of these dates is true. Each answers a different question. Mixing them up is a common mistake. A careful reader always asks: first what, and in which *institution*?

words.d: an object made by people long ago, like a painting or a tool
a lasting group with its own rules, like a school, league or association

look.title: First What?

look.prompt: How could you rewrite the hallway sign so it is accurate?

check.why: 1937 is the year of the first IHSA state wrestling champions.

check.why: An institution is a lasting group, like a school or association, with rules.

check.q: Which is the best question to ask about any 'first' date?
choices: First what, and in which institution?
check.why: A first date only makes sense when we know what began and in which group.

lessons.title: Girls Join the State Finals
lessons.mainIdea: Illinois girls wrestling held its first IHSA state finals in 2022, eighty-five years after the boys.
reading: For most of IHSA history, the state wrestling tournament was for boys only. Some girls wrestled on boys teams over the years. But there was no separate girls state title in Illinois.

That changed in the 2021–22 school year. The IHSA held its first girls wrestling *state finals* in 2022. Girls now had their own weight classes and their own champions. Other states had started girls tournaments too.

The gap between 1937 and 2022 is eighty-five years. That gap shows that a sport can exist long before everyone is let into its *championship*. Dates of new doors are part of history, just like dates of first titles.

words.d: the last rounds of a state tournament, where champions are decided
a contest that decides the official winner of a sport or event

lessons.title: Reading a Tournament Record
lessons.mainIdea: Programs, newspapers and association lists are sources, and each shows something different.
reading: A *primary source* is a record made at the time of an event. A 1937 program is one. A newspaper story from the next morning is another. Historians use primary sources to check what happened.

Each source shows something different. A program printed before a meet lists who entered. A newspaper report tells who won and how many people came. An IHSA champions list gives the names that the association made official.

Sometimes sources disagree about a spelling or a score. Then historians compare them. A careful *record* keeps the name, the school, the weight and the year together. Good records let people today find the wrestlers of 1937.

words.d: a record made at the time of an event, like a program or a newspaper
a written list or account that keeps facts for later
